raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a standalone `sglang-kernel` install next to a different PyTorch than it was built against, `import sgl_kernel` fails with `undefined symbol: c10::MessageLogger...`. That looks like a GPU-arch problem, so #29317 was filed as a "missing SM121 wheel" — but the wheel does contain `sm_121a`. The real cause is a PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch.

Docker and `pip install sglang` pin PyTorch to 2.11, so they aren't affected; this only hits the standalone-wheel + mismatched-torch case. #26598 is the long-term fix. Until then, this makes the error say the torch version is mismatched, so it stops getting misread as a missing arch.

## Modifications

- `load_utils.py`: on an `undefined symbol` failure, name the installed torch and the missing symbol instead of a generic reinstall/arch message.
- `load_utils.py` / `__init__.py`: add `load_common_ops()`; with `SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS` set it warns and returns `None` instead of raising (debug only — kernels still raise if called).
- `tests/test_load_utils.py`: cover the ABI message, the non-ABI case, and the flag.
- `faq.mdx`: document the mismatch and the working install paths.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — import-path only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests — `tests/test_load_utils.py`
- [x] Update documentation — `faq.mdx`
- [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks — N/A
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance

## Notes

- `SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS` uses `os.environ` since `sgl_kernel` can't import `sglang.srt.environ`; matches the existing `SGLANG_KERNEL_API_LOGLEVEL`.
- The flag is debug-only; it doesn't make a model serve on a mismatched install.

Refs #29317. Complements #26598.

nodes.body:
> Why can we not add SM121 to the kernel archs

After looking into this, I made several changes to the PR. Turns out, the published cu130 aarch64 wheel already contains `sm_121a`:

```
$ cuobjdump sgl_kernel/sm100/common_ops.abi3.so | grep -oE 'sm_[0-9]+[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
  56 sm_90   56 sm_100a   56 sm_103a   56 sm_110a   56 sm_120a   56 sm_121a
```

(`sm90/`/`sm100/` are fast-math vs precise-math variants — both carry the full set.) `sm_121a` is at `CMakeLists.txt:222`, gated on CUDA ≥ 13.0 + aarch64. So the GB10 crash isn't a missing arch — it's a libtorch C++ ABI mismatch at import (`undefined symbol: c10::MessageLogger::stream[abi:cxx11]()`): the standalone wheel is built against torch 2.11.0 but declares `dependencies = []`, so it links against whatever torch is present. Across cu130/aarch64 torch builds only 2.11.0 imports; a source build against the installed torch works (incl. 2.13). I've reframed this PR around diagnosing that mismatch.

On your actual question, one gencode list does still lack SM121: `INFLLM_FLASH_CUDA_FLAGS` (`CMakeLists.txt:513-517`) emits only `sm_90` + `sm_120a`, and `infllm_ops` installs unconditionally (line 541), so on GB10 it has no loadable code (sm_120a is arch-exclusive to sm120, and there's no PTX for a JIT fallback). I confirmed the InfLLM kernels _do_ compile for `sm_121a` (they're generic SM80 FlashAttention kernels), so it looks like an "add the arch" fix rather than a guard-out. InfLLM-v2 (#29383) postdates the published v0.4.4 wheel (2026-06-17) so it didn't cause this issue. I can look into it separately.

Separately, a policy question for the wheel: would you want `sglang-kernel` to declare its build-target torch (e.g. inject `Requires-Dist: torch==<build version>` at build time) so pip refuses a mismatched torch up front, or keep it dependency-free by design? Happy to follow up with that change if you'd prefer the build-time declaration.

Hi, could you please use your own words, since that's easier than reading the output of AI, which can be really verbose

Second, we don't guarantee any PyTorch compatibility on sgl-kernel. When using Docker or pip, the PyTorch is pinned to 2.11

For compatibility with different torch versions, there is https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26598. So is this PR still needed?

My main goal with this PR was to improve the error message. The linked issue #29317 got filed as a missing SM121 wheel because the current undefined symbol error looks like an arch problem. This PR would cut out a lot of confusion by having the error explicitly state the torch version mismatch while #26598 is being worked on.

Thanks @layahaasini. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a fallback mechanism for `sgl_kernel` when prebuilt binaries are missing for specific GPU architectures (such as NVIDIA GB10 / SM121). It allows the import to succeed with a warning when the environment variable `SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS=1` is set, enabling models that rely on Triton/PyTorch fallbacks to run. The review feedback suggests improving the robustness of this fallback by supporting case-insensitive boolean parsing for the environment variable and using a dummy object instead of `None` to raise descriptive errors when missing operators are accessed.

> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

+### `import sgl_kernel` fails with `undefined symbol`
+
+If `import sgl_kernel` (or server startup) fails with an error like `undefined symbol: c10::MessageLogger::stream[abi:cxx11]()`, this is a PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch, not a missing GPU architecture. The prebuilt `sgl_kernel` wheel is compiled against one PyTorch version and does not link against a different one, because PyTorch does not guarantee C++ ABI compatibility across versions.

 import logging

+import warnings

@@ -165,6 +166,31 @@ def _load_architecture_specific_ops():
         f"- {type(err).__name__}: {err}" for err in previous_import_errors
     )
 
+    # An "undefined symbol" load error means a symbol is missing from the loaded
+    # native libraries -- most often a PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch, sometimes CUDA/cuDNN --
+    # not a missing GPU build. Surface that instead of a reinstall/arch red herring (#29317).
+    if any("undefined symbol" in str(err) for err in previous_import_errors):
+        abi_error_msg = f"""
+[sgl_kernel] Failed to load compiled kernels: a required symbol is missing from the
+loaded native libraries (see the symbol under "Original load errors" below).
+
+This is most often a PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch -- common_ops was built against a
+different PyTorch than the installed torch {torch.__version__}, and PyTorch does not
+guarantee C++ ABI stability across versions. It can also indicate a CUDA/cuDNN
+mismatch. It is not a missing GPU architecture.
+
+To fix a PyTorch ABI mismatch, match the torch version: install the torch build this
+sgl_kernel was compiled against, use the matching NGC container
+(nvcr.io/nvidia/sglang), or build sgl_kernel from source against your installed torch.
+
+GPU compute capability: {compute_capability} | CUDA: {torch.version.cuda}
+
+Original load errors:
+{attempt_error_msg}
+"""
+        logger.debug(abi_error_msg)
+        raise ImportError(abi_error_msg)
+
     # All attempts failed
     cuda_version = torch.version.cuda
     if cuda_version and cuda_version.startswith("12"):
@@ -197,6 +223,36 @@ def _load_architecture_specific_ops():
     raise ImportError(error_msg)
 
 
+def load_common_ops():
+    """Load the compiled common_ops, or None if SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS is set.
+
+    On failure the diagnostic ImportError from _load_architecture_specific_ops is
+    raised (an ABI-mismatch message when the .so is present but a symbol is missing).
+    SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS=1 downgrades it to a warning and returns None so
+    import can proceed -- a debug escape hatch; kernels backed by sgl_kernel then raise
+    if called. Read via os.environ, not sglang.srt.environ, since sgl_kernel is a
+    standalone package that cannot import sglang.
+    """
+    allow_missing = os.environ.get("SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS", "0").lower() in (
+        "1",
+        "true",
+        "yes",
+        "on",
+    )
+    try:
+        return _load_architecture_specific_ops()
+    except ImportError:
+        if not allow_missing:
+            raise
+        warnings.warn(
+            "[sgl_kernel] common_ops failed to load and SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS "
+            "is set; continuing without it. Kernels backed by sgl_kernel will raise if called.",
+            RuntimeWarning,
+            stacklevel=2,
+        )
+        return None
+
+
 # copy & modify from torch/utils/cpp_extension.py
 def _find_cuda_home():
     """Find the CUDA install path."""

@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+import builtins
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+from sgl_kernel import load_utils
+
+UNDEFINED_SYMBOL_ERR = "undefined symbol: _ZN3c1013MessageLogger6streamB5cxx11Ev"
+GENERIC_ERR = "libfoo.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
+
+
+def _force_load_failure(monkeypatch, load_error):
+    # A common_ops .so is "found" but fails to load with load_error, and the final
+    # `import common_ops` fallback fails -- so _load_architecture_specific_ops reaches
+    # its error branch with load_error recorded.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        load_utils.glob,
+        "glob",
+        lambda pattern: ["/nonexistent/sm100/common_ops.abi3.so"],
+    )
+
+    def _raise(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise ImportError(load_error)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(load_utils.importlib.util, "spec_from_file_location", _raise)
+
+    real_import = builtins.__import__
+
+    def _no_common_ops(name, *args, **kwargs):
+        if name == "common_ops":
+            raise ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'common_ops'")
+        return real_import(name, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(builtins, "__import__", _no_common_ops)
+
+
+def _raise_undef():
+    raise ImportError(UNDEFINED_SYMBOL_ERR)
+
+
+def test_undefined_symbol_raises_abi_diagnostic(monkeypatch):
+    _force_load_failure(monkeypatch, UNDEFINED_SYMBOL_ERR)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ImportError) as excinfo:
+        load_utils._load_architecture_specific_ops()
+
+    msg = str(excinfo.value)
+    assert "PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch" in msg
+    assert "undefined symbol" in msg
+
+
+def test_non_abi_failure_keeps_generic_message(monkeypatch):
+    # A load failure that is NOT an undefined symbol must not be mislabeled an ABI
+    # mismatch -- it routes to the generic message.
+    _force_load_failure(monkeypatch, GENERIC_ERR)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ImportError) as excinfo:
+        load_utils._load_architecture_specific_ops()
+
+    msg = str(excinfo.value)
+    assert "PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch" not in msg
+    assert "Could not load any common_ops" in msg
+
+
+def test_load_common_ops_reraises_without_flag(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(load_utils, "_load_architecture_specific_ops", _raise_undef)
+    monkeypatch.delenv("SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS", raising=False)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ImportError):
+        load_utils.load_common_ops()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["0", "false", "no", "off", ""])
+def test_load_common_ops_reraises_for_falsey_flag(monkeypatch, value):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(load_utils, "_load_architecture_specific_ops", _raise_undef)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS", value)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ImportError):
+        load_utils.load_common_ops()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "true", "YES", "on"])
+def test_load_common_ops_allows_missing_with_flag(monkeypatch, value):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(load_utils, "_load_architecture_specific_ops", _raise_undef)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS", value)
+
+    with pytest.warns(RuntimeWarning):
+        assert load_utils.load_common_ops() is None
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

I confirmed the InfLLM kernels _do_ compile for `sm_121a` (they're generic SM80 FlashAttention kernels), so it looks like an "add the arch" fix rather than a guard-out. InfLLM-v2 (#29383) postdates the published v0.4.4 wheel (2026-06-17) so it didn't cause this issue. I can look into it separately.

Separately, a policy question for the wheel: would you want `sglang-kernel` to declare its build-target torch (e.g. inject `Requires-Dist: torch==<build version>` at build time) so pip refuses a mismatched torch up front, or keep it dependency-free by design? Happy to follow up with that change if you'd prefer the build-time declaration.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a fallback mechanism for `sgl_kernel` when prebuilt binaries are missing for specific GPU architectures (such as NVIDIA GB10 / SM121). It allows the import to succeed with a warning when the environment variable `SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS=1` is set, enabling models that rely on Triton/PyTorch fallbacks to run. The review feedback suggests improving the robustness of this fallback by supporting case-insensitive boolean parsing for the environment variable and using a dummy object instead of `None` to raise descriptive errors when missing operators are accessed.
